after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}+4x-7=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$   Find $p+q.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4x-7 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+4x & =7 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 2\cdot x & =7 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 2\cdot x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2} & =7 \\ (x+2)^{2}-4 & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)^{2}-4 & =7 \\ (x+2)^{2} & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=2,$ $q=11,$ and $p+q=13.$

decision.explanation: The equation is (x-1)^2=1, so p=-1 and q=1, giving pq=-1. Its roots are x=0 and x=2, whose sum is 2.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-2x+1=1$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,pq\,,$ and the sum of the roots ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+1 & =1 \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot x\cdot 1+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}-{1}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=-1$ and $q=1.$ Thus, $pq=-1.$

We now solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =1 \\ \sqrt{(x-1)^{2}} & =\sqrt{1} \\ |x-1| & =1 \\ x-1 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =1\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =1-1=0 \\ {x}_{2} & =1+1=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2.$

The equation x2−2x+1=1 can be written in the form (x+p)2=q. Find pq, and the sum of the roots x1+x2.

a
pq=1 and x1+x2=2
b
pq=−1 and x1+x2=1
c
pq=0 and x1+x2=2

EXPLANATION

First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side: x2−2x+1=1x2−2x=0x2−2⋅x⋅1+12−12=0(x−1)2−12=0(x−1)2=1

Hence, p=−1 and q=1. Thus, pq=−1.

We now solve the equation using the square root method: (x−1)2=1(x−1)2=1|x−1|=1x−1=±1x=1±1

We simplify the two solutions: x1=1−1=0x2=1+1=2

Therefore, the sum is x1+x2=2.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Quadratic Equation When the Solutions Are Rational
content.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-2x+1=1$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,pq\,,$ and the sum of the roots ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+1 & =1 \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot x\cdot 1+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}-{1}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=-1$ and $q=1.$ Thus, $pq=-1.$

We now solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =1 \\ \sqrt{(x-1)^{2}} & =\sqrt{1} \\ |x-1| & =1 \\ x-1 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =1\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =1-1=0 \\ {x}_{2} & =1+1=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2.$

$$

$$
